newsitem.title: PORTUGAL: Portugal's AutoEuropa to halt production Friday.
newsitem.headline: Portugal's AutoEuropa to halt production Friday.

text.p: Portugal's biggest car manufacturer, the Ford-Volkswagen AutoEuropa joint venture, will halt production on Friday because the French truckers' strike had disrupted supplies to the plant, a spokeswoman said.
"Production will be halted tomorrow, but the factory will remain open for maintenance," Carmo Jardim told Reuters.
She said a decision whether to halt production next week would depend on events in France. The AutoEuropa plant, 30 miles (50 km) south of Lisbon, is normally shut over the weekend.

AutoEuropa, which produces 510 passenger vans per day mainly for export to Europe, had been paying an additional 50 million escudos ($330,000) per day since November 20 to fly supplies to the plant that were normally brought by road, Jardim said.
She said the supplies brought by chartered aircraft included engines, transmissions and air conditioning components.
Exports from AutoEuropa, the biggest foreign investment in Portugal, were not affected as most finished vehicles were transported by train and boat.
Striking truck drivers voted to keep up their 11-day stranglehold on the French economy on Thursday, defying government calls to return to work after talks with bosses collapsed over pay demands.
